h3State.failing: form.fill returns the generic 'The OCADE extension could not complete that request.' — which is the catch-all in onMessageExternal, meaning handle() THREW rather than refusing.
h3State.diagnosis: ensureOriginPermission calls chrome.permissions.request from inside the message handler. That API requires a user activation, and a service worker handling an external message has none, so it throws instead of returning false. Granting the origin from the popup beforehand is the correct sequence, but the popup grant in the harness returned false while the same call in isolation returned {granted:true} and flipped permissions.contains from false to true.
h3State.whyThisMattersBeyondTheTest: If chrome.permissions.request throws in the handler rather than returning false, a user who has not pre-granted an origin gets a generic failure instead of 'You didn't grant OCADE access to this site.' The refusal path that exists in the code at line 805 is unreachable in that case. That is a product defect worth fixing, not only a harness problem.
h3State.nextStep: Grant the origin from the popup with Runtime.evaluate userGesture and assert permissions.contains returns true BEFORE sending form.fill; if the grant still returns false inside the full harness, compare against the isolated repro which succeeded, since the only differences are the number of open targets and the timing.

environmentNotes.headlessCannotGrantPermissions: Under --headless=new the extension consent prompt is auto-denied and chrome.permissions.request returns false. H3 onwards must run headful. Measured, not assumed.
environmentNotes.loadExtensionFlagIsDead: --load-extension is ignored by Chrome 137+ and by Edge. CDP Extensions.loadUnpacked with --enable-unsafe-extension-debugging is the working route and needs no policy change.
environmentNotes.serviceWorkerStateIsVolatile: pairingCode and pairingToken are module-level state in an MV3 service worker. Pair immediately before use; anything that waits for a real site to load will find the worker restarted and the pairing gone.
environmentNotes.originPinningIsReal: externally_connectable pins to caeracadane.com, localhost and 127.0.0.1. A controlled site cannot message the extension — the controlling origin and the controlled tab are deliberately different, and the extension acts on a tab named by tabId.

noOwnerActionRequired: Unlike the earlier browser-control blocker, nothing here waits on the owner. H3-H5 are ordinary remaining work.
